I think it would be better if the default behaviour of Import Module, let's say Import Mathlib only pulled in the definitions that that are in the top-scope of Mathlib and not under any Mathlib.Tactic.*. Then, if the user truly wanted to import all of it, perhaps we could force them to type Import Mathlib.* explicitly. I, again, imported Mathlib without truly wanting it and now I can either try to forcefully quit the building process or wait infinitely long for it to finish.

What do you think?

If you're building mathlib on your computer, something went wrong in a previous step. You should not need to do so. Can you (1) close VS Code (and check there are no Lean processes running on your computer), (2) delete the .lake directory in your project (for extra caution), (3) open the project again, (4) click on the forall symbol in the top right and fetch the mathlib cache? Wait for that step to complete, then you should not need to build mathlib yourself.
(Mathlib has hardly any file in the top-level scope, so I don't see how your proposal would help with this.)

Okay, that worked - after manually clicking fetch cache, it fetched successfully and after Restart File, no build was running. Is it expected from the user to click Fetch Cache in every Mathlib project or should that be happening by default somehow? Asking to verify if I should proceed to write steps to reproduce bug, or just ignore that

Different projects are very likely to be using different versions of mathlib (mathlib updated 1218 times this month already, so on average 40 times per day) so yes you have to fetch mathlib cache on a per-project basis.

Let me rephrase my question - don’t we want Lean to try to ‚lake exe cache get’ by default when running ‚lake build’ ? Assuming Mathlib version is properly declared in ‚lakefile.toml’, and it is the same version I have already used locally, is there a good reason for user to have to remember to run ‚cache get’ manually?

With the new cache integrated into Lake, we will move towards more automatic and fine-grained fetching but the automated part will need to go through some testing rounds before being enabled for everyone to make sure there are no negative side effects. So, we're working on it.

Additionally, even before the improvements to the Lake cache, if you are using the 'Build Project' command in VS Code (Forall menu > Project actions > Build project), it will ensure that the Mathlib cache is fetched before building.

don’t we want Lean to try to ‚lake exe cache get’ by default when running ‚lake build’ ?

No please don't, accessing the network when the user just asked to build something is not okay without an opt-in. Surprising behavior is usually bad behavior. The user just asked for a build.

No please don't, accessing the network when the user just asked to build something is not okay without an opt-in. Surprising behavior is usually bad behavior. The user just asked for a build.

But isn't this already standard practice? Package managers like uv automatically download all dependencies when you run uv run main.py. I mean lake already does this when it downloads git repositories.

However, I would expect that if you run lake build twice in a row without modifying the lake manifest or pulling new commits then the second lake build would not access the network.

Snir Broshi said:

No please don't, accessing the network when the user just asked to build something is not okay without an opt-in.

Wait -- are you claiming that lake currently never attempts to access the network after lake build? My memory is that sometimes lake build fails for me on the subway with some complaint about how github.com can't be accessed.

Niels Voss said:

No please don't, accessing the network when the user just asked to build something is not okay without an opt-in. Surprising behavior is usually bad behavior. The user just asked for a build.

But isn't this already standard practice? Package managers like uv automatically download all dependencies when you run uv run main.py. I mean lake already does this when it downloads git repositories.

Sure but that's the purpose of uv run, users of uv know that's what they're getting. I like uv, but if I want to run a python file I'll just do python ./main.py. If OTOH I want to install dependencies and then run a file, I'll use uv run.
So there should be a command I can run that just builds a Lean project, and lake build is probably the sensible choice for such a command, and not lake build --local-cache-only or something.
A better example would be docker build, that for some strange reasons sometimes tries to pull the base image and sometimes doesn't.
... and such failures are really annoying!

Snir Broshi said:

Sure but that's the purpose of uv run, users of uv know that's what they're getting. I like uv, but if I want to run a python file I'll just do python ./main.py. If OTOH I want to install dependencies and then run a file, I'll use uv run.

Theoretically, lake lean main.lean is the parallel of uv run main.lean and lean main.lean is the parallel of python main.py. The odd part is that lake build can faill in between these as Lean requires building to import local modules whereas Python does not.

What would be your desired behavior of lake build if you just added mathlib to your lakefile.toml and it hasn't been downloaded yet?

I haven't thought this through, but I think I'd like it to error if it finds a mathlib import, similar to how import numpy would error in python if you didn't uv install.
Then you'd run lake update, which would fetch Mathlib and Mathlib's cache.
And similar to uv add or npm install ..., I think a lake add Mathlib command would be nice, that both edits lakefile.toml and downloads Mathlib and the cache.

Although it might be okay for lake build to do this itself if dependencies are missing, similar to cargo build. I'm not sure.

Kevin Buzzard ha dicho:

Snir Broshi said:

No please don't, accessing the network when the user just asked to build something is not okay without an opt-in.

Wait -- are you claiming that lake currently never attempts to access the network after lake build? My memory is that sometimes lake build fails for me on the subway with some complaint about how github.com can't be accessed.

lake build accesses the network if it doesn't have the required dependencies. That makes sense to me. It should not access the network otherwise.

I agree, but also I believe Kevin references #general > lake exe cache get failure with no internet where not only lake exe cache get doesn't work offline, but neither do lake exe cache unpack or lake build, and possibly every lake command requires internet.
Although I still think requiring a lake update even when there are missing dependencies is saner than lake build doing it, or at least it should ask for confirmation beforehand (or fail if the tty isn't interactive, e.g. in CI).

I think there are two questions getting mixed up here:

  • A: If I don't have mathlib (the source files), should lake build download it? I think here everyone says yes.
  • B: If I have mathlib (source files) but not yet the cache, should lake build get the cache? I think @Paweł Balawender 🇵🇱 would have liked that, but @Snir Broshi is against it to make sure lake build still works offline if it has a chance of working?

In A the download is necessary to build, in B it is "only" nice to have / to speed things up. And I think the analogy with tools like uv (or cargo build and stack build) works for A, but not for B because those other packet managers or languages don't also have a cache for each library. Right?

Also, I think lake update should not be the (commonly used) command to get the cache because afaik it may update dependencies and the lean version used to newer versions. I have seen people get bitten by this, especially when working in non-mathlib projects supposed to be sticking on different lean versions than current mathlib.

Malvin Gattinger said:

  • A: If I don't have mathlib (the source files), should lake build download it? I think here everyone says yes.

But I repeatedly said no

Malvin Gattinger said:

Snir Broshi is against it to make sure lake build still works offline if it has a chance of working?

No, working offline is beside the point (even though it's still important). Predictable behavior and separation of concerns is.

Malvin Gattinger said:

Also, I think lake update should not be the (commonly used) command to get the cache because afaik it may update dependencies and the lean version used to newer versions. I have seen people get bitten by this

Right, that's exactly the point. A command should do what it says on the tin.
But when it's downloading Mathlib, I think downloading the cache as well is fine, since the cache can be considered a part of the "bundle" when installing.

I think there are two questions getting mixed up here:

  • A: If I don't have mathlib (the source files), should lake build download it? I think here everyone says yes.
  • B: If I have mathlib (source files) but not yet the cache, should lake build get the cache? I think Paweł Balawender 🇵🇱 would have liked that, but Snir Broshi is against it to make sure lake build still works offline if it has a chance of working?

In A the download is necessary to build, in B it is "only" nice to have / to speed things up. And I think the analogy with tools like uv (or cargo build and stack build) works for A, but not for B because those other packet managers or languages don't also have a cache for each library. Right?

In my opinion, for projects that depend on mathlib, the cache should be downloaded at the exact same time as mathlib is itself being downloaded. (I don't know how this should work for those working on mathlib itself). This way, lake build will access the internet no more often than it does right now.
That should already be happening, though.

This just randomly happened to me, this is not okay
lake-help.mp4

i.e. any lake command automatically tries to install the active toolchain, including an innocent lake --help. elan show says:

active toolchain
----------------

leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0 (resolved from default 'stable')
(toolchain will be installed on first use)

What would you rather it do? Recall that the list of lake commands is version dependent, so lake --help requires downloading lake to give a useful message. This behavior is very similar to the gradle wrapper command ./gradlew.

Niels Voss said:

What would you rather it do?

Error: the active toolchain 'leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0' is not installed.
Run `elan toolchain install 'leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0'` to install it or
use `elan` to switch to a different toolchain.

It can also ask the user whether to install it. The current behavior seems malicious.
See also #lean4 > Stop lean automatically downloading things to my computer @ 💬 (where you also suggested prompting).

Niels Voss said:

This behavior is very similar to the gradle wrapper command ./gradlew.

I think Java is the last place we should be taking inspiration from, and gradlew in particular. It's awful for all sorts of reasons, one of which is that it randomly downloads things but never when you want it to.

It can also ask the user whether to install it. The current behavior seems malicious.

This is a good idea. I think there could be a y/n prompt right before downloading, and this could be configurable. I would not call the current behavior "malicious", but I can see why it might not be desirable. Note basically all Lean projects have a lean-toolchain file (I was surprised to find out that that this was actually optional) so we can just have it default to that.

I think Java is the last place we should be taking inspiration from, and gradlew in particular. It's awful for all sorts of reasons, one of which is that it randomly downloads things but never when you want it to.

I actually like Java, but we can agree to disagree. But do you take issue with gradle, or specifically the gradle wrapper? The wrapper has pros and cons but it isn't that bad of an idea.
